title_pattern.notes: Title carries zero curiosity; discovery is purely via the For You feed and the first-frame burned-in caption, which IS the real title ('There's a killer hiding in our apartment complex'). Hashtags mislabel it as anime to ride anime-edit traffic. For our use: put the hook sentence as the first caption, keep the post caption short with niche tags.

thumbnail.composition: Auto cover = frame 0. Black 9:16 frame; landscape image band in the middle (~y 29-71%); two-line white italic caption sitting on the black above the band. Subject centred in a one-point-perspective corridor vanishing point.
thumbnail.text: 'Theres a killer hiding in our apartment complex Every' - white italic sans (Arial-italic look), ~4% frame height, centred, no stroke/box, cut mid-sentence
thumbnail.colours: Sick teal/green corridor lighting, near-black shadow figure, a single dark-red door frame on the right as accent; surround pure black
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Small-to-mid figure (~45% of band height) dwarfed by long corridor; knife raised above head; the vanishing point light frames the head
thumbnail.why_it_works: Instantly legible threat (silhouette + knife + grin) in a relatable place (your apartment hallway); the caption states the premise in plain words; the cut-off 'Every' pulls you into the next line. Teal-on-black reads as horror in a feed thumbnail grid.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: There's a killer hiding in our apartment complex. Every time they strike, a song plays in the hallway. Sometimes sad, sometimes intense.
hook.verbatim_5_to_13s: Management sent a group text telling everyone to lock their doors, then updated us shortly after that the killer had been caught. Just then, someone knocked.
hook.device: First-person cold open stating a dangerous premise in the first sentence + one uncanny rule (a song plays when they strike) for specificity; then a false-relief beat ('killer had been caught') immediately undercut by a knock at 11.2 s. Classic 'safe -> knock' reversal; no intro, no channel branding.

beats.summary: Killer hiding in my apartment complex; a song plays in the hallway every time they strike.
Group text: lock doors... then 'killer caught'. Immediately someone knocks.
Cop at peephole asks to open; protagonist notices wrong details: cop alone (cops work in pairs), four creepy smiley stickers on chest. Chill.
Exactly four accounts confirmed the capture: admin Zhang Bo plus three instant replies (601, 502, 301) urging cooperation. 'Way too coincidental.'
Other neighbours (1002, 601) question it; nobody answers them.
Cop senses something, pounds the door, threatens to break it, radios 'Unit 802 uncooperative, requesting backup'.
Chat erupts: the four accounts tag him by name, call him paranoid, admin says police have the landlord's number and keys are coming.
He deduces the four accounts' owners are already dead and the killer is using their phones to lure him out. 'Rather arrested than murdered.'
No signal for 911, WeChat messages fail with red marks; yet the building group chat still works. Weird.
Li from 601 warns 'don't open, that's not the police', sees red footprints in elevator; admin deletes it and mutes the whole group.
Too-good sublease with free rent; previous tenant borrowed his phone at signing - likely planted malware. Why all the trouble?
Rhythmic knocking becomes kicking; they're breaking in.
Remembers the box the previous tenant left: burner phone, one bar of battery. Swaps SIM, dials police.
Real police: signal is jammed, how did you reach us; 30 seconds of battery; 'do not open the door, it's a whole crew of serial killers'. Asks if building manager is alive.
Real building manager is at the perimeter and is a different person (a middle-aged woman) - the 'manager' in the chat is fake.
Phone dies; last notification: 'Don't let them find you. Get out of the building.' No resolution (part-2 / comment bait).

pacing.wpm_note: Very fast narration (~4.4 words/s), essentially no pauses; captions chunk 4-9 words per line
pacing.shots_estimated: ~70 distinct visual states (counting each chat-screen update); 51 shot groups listed
pacing.avg_shot_note: Character shots hold 2-6 s; chat-screen sequences hold one framing for 10-25 s but refresh every ~2-4 s via new bubbles, so perceived change is ~every 2-3 s
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: new anomaly/escalation roughly every 12-20 s (pairs, stickers, exactly four, pounding, radio, tags, dead-owners theory, no signal, warning, mute, malware, kicking, burner phone, 30 s, wrong manager, final notification)

techniques_worth_copying: Open with the premise as a single first-person sentence plus one weird rule; false relief then a knock inside 12 s
'Count the clue' deduction: a concrete number (exactly four accounts / four stickers) makes the viewer feel clever and creates the mid-video theory
Group-chat-as-antagonist: the story is told through phone message screens with names + unit numbers; cheap to render, highly readable, lets one narrator voice all characters
Escalation ladder with external pressure (door pounding, backup, landlord keys) alternating with information beats (chat), every 12-20 s
Isolation beats: no signal, failed messages, then the one channel still working is the compromised one
Ally warning that gets deleted/muted on screen - visible censorship is a strong horror signal
Flashback in a different palette (bright beige vs present-day blue/teal) to plant 'it was a setup' backstory
Ticking clock device in the final third (one battery bar, '30 seconds' graphic)
Twist via authority confirmation (real police: the manager is someone else) then hard cliffhanger on a phone notification - drives comments/part 2
Fixed letterbox layout: black 9:16 with centred image band and captions above it keeps captions out of UI and makes every frame consistent
Fast 260 wpm continuous narration over low music bed; no pauses = no scroll-away gaps
code_only_remake_needs: Layout template: 1080x1920 black canvas, 1080x~720 image band centred (y≈560-1360), caption line(s) above the band in white italic sans, word-chunk timed to TTS

Character kit (SVG): round white-head stick/bean figures with hair variants, blue shirt protagonist, grey 'shadow' killer variant with grin; poses: back-view at door, peeking, holding phone, phone to ear, kneeling, shocked (sweat drops, motion ticks); cop/operator with peaked cap + headset; expression swaps (eyes/mouth) are enough

Background kit: dark corridor (one-point perspective), front door with peephole + lock, dark living room, bedroom with lamp, bright flashback room; posterized/flat with teal/blue grading via SVG filters or gradient overlays; vignette

Phone UI component: big flat grey cartoon hand holding a phone; group-chat screen with header, avatars, name + unit labels, message bubbles that pop in (spring), @-mentions, red failed-send '!', grey muted/deleted state; burner candy-bar phone variant with keypad + battery bar + notification text

Effects: slow Ken-Burns push-ins on every shot, small screen shake for knocks/kicks, whip-blur transition, crossfades for flashback, door impact cracks/motion lines, peephole fisheye mask, pop-in countdown graphic, floating music-note icons
Audio: one fast narrator TTS (Kokoro, ~250 wpm) + low drone/tension loop + knock/kick SFX; all character lines in narrator voice keeps TTS simple
Storyboard granularity: ~1 visual per sentence (2-4 s), chat sequences as single shots with per-message timed reveals
Original story needed: our own locked-room + compromised-chat premise; do not reuse this plot, names or art
